title: Vaineau, Barachant & Andreev 2013 — Brain Invaders Adaptive versus Non-Adaptive P300 Brain-Computer Interface dataset (BI2013a)
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic recordings from 24 healthy subjects performing a visual P300 brain-computer interface task based on the Brain Invaders video game. The study compares adaptive versus non-adaptive calibration approaches using Riemannian geometry for classifier training. EEG data were acquired using 16 electrodes at 512 Hz sampling rate during sessions conducted at GIPSA-lab in 2013, with each subject completing 8 sessions containing both training and online phases.
methods_description: EEG recordings were acquired using 16 wet Silver/Silver Chloride electrodes (standard 10-20 montage) with a g.USBamp amplifier (g.tec) at 512 Hz sampling rate. Reference electrode was placed at left earlobe with ground at FZ. Subjects performed a visual P300 task using the Brain Invaders interface with 36 symbols organized in 12 groups. Each session contained two runs (adaptive and non-adaptive, randomized order) with training phases (80 target and 400 non-target flashes) and variable online phases. Data were recorded without digital filtering, with 50 Hz line frequency.
